column3: Summary
[EP-00] Foundations
column11: Monorepo, AWS environments, data schema, auth, app shells, design system, media, notifications, live updates, background jobs and search: the plumbing every feature needs.

column3: [EP-01] Accounts, profiles and verification
column11: Sign-up with one role, profiles for each role, privacy, block and report, provider portfolios.

column3: [EP-02] Events and discovery
column11: Organisers create and publish events; consumers search, follow, mark Going and hear about changes.

column3: [EP-03] Promotion feed and sharing
column11: Organiser posts and reels, the feed, likes and comments, and sharing out to WhatsApp and Instagram.

column3: [EP-04] Hiring marketplace
column11: Provider search, booking requests, job posts, quotes, confirmed bookings, cancellation and completion.

column3: [EP-05] Stalls
column11: Stall slots, applications, invitations, stall numbers and the stall list on the event page.

column3: [EP-06] Reviews and ranking
column11: Four-way reviews tied to real jobs or Going marks, rank score, tier badges and leaderboards.

column3: [EP-07] Venue maps
column11: The map builder and one versioned map format; floor plans from an image, a PDF, a blank grid or a saved venue map; labelled pins, zones and stall listings; the interactive 2D map; an AI first draft; and an offline copy in the app.

column3: [EP-08] Community
column11: Event boards and group chats, topic and city communities, friends.

column3: [EP-09] Messaging and notifications
column11: 1:1 chat, event Q&A, announcements and transactional notifications.

column3: [EP-10] Organiser dashboard
column11: Live interest counts, analytics and the hiring tracker for each event.

column3: [EP-11] Administration, trust and safety
column11: Verification, report queue, fake events, disputes, review moderation, communities and the audit log.

column3: [EP-12] Quality, privacy and release
column11: Languages, PDPA, accessibility, performance, security, usability testing and pilot readiness.

column3: [EP-13] Ticketing (after the ATP)
column11: Kept so the backlog is complete. No tasks until the ticketing phase is planned.

column3: [EP-14] Sandbox payments
column11: Payments on the PayHere sandbox, straight to each payee's own account: deposits and instalments, stall fees, cancellation fees and refunds, receipts with the commission line. No real money moves in the ATP.

column3: [EN-01-T1] Finish the pnpm + Turborepo monorepo (Tezera-LK/tezera): apps/api (NestJS), apps/web (Next.js), amplify/ (auth only), infra/ (AWS CDK), packages/shared, apps/mobile (Flutter, proposed); strict TypeScript, ESLint, Prettier
[EN-01-T2] Shared package with Zod schemas and TypeScript types used by the NestJS API and the Next.js portal (the Flutter app uses the generated API client, EN-05)
[EN-01-T3] GitHub Actions CI on every pull request: install, lint, type-check and test the TypeScript apps; flutter analyze and flutter test for the app
[EN-01-T4] Test setup: Jest for the NestJS API and shared code, with a PostgreSQL test database in Docker; Flutter widget tests; Playwright for the portal
[EN-01-T5] Pull request template and branch protection on main
[EN-02-T1] Amplify Hosting connected to the Git repository: the Next.js portal and the Amplify auth backend deploy from the dev and main branches, each stage with its own Cognito pool in ap-south-1
[EN-02-T2] Pull request previews for the portal on Amplify Hosting, pointed at the dev API
[EN-02-T3] Local set-up documented in the README: PostgreSQL in Docker (port 5433), the API on port 4000, and an ampx sandbox for each developer's own Cognito pool

[EN-02-T4] Secrets per stage in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store (SecureString) or Secrets Manager: database URL, Dialog e-SMS keys, FCM key; the Lambda reads them at start; documented .env.example for local settings
[EN-02-T5] Flutter builds for Android and iOS: debug builds for the team and internal distribution (Firebase App Distribution and TestFlight, proposed)
[EN-02-T6] AWS account: an IAM login per team member with MFA required (tezera-require-mfa policy), root account locked away, AWS Budgets alert (proposed)

[EN-02-T7] CDK api-stack fixes (infra/lib/api-stack.ts): Cognito pool and client IDs for each stage, the database URL read from Parameter Store, class-validator and class-transformer bundled, timeout and memory checked against cold starts
[EN-02-T8] Prisma in the Lambda bundle: the linux-arm64 engine and schema.prisma copied by a CDK command hook; GET /health/db passes on the deployed dev stage (not verified)
[EN-02-T9] Deploy the CDK api-stack from CI: dev on merge to dev, main on release; prisma migrate deploy runs before the new Lambda goes live (proposed)
[EN-03-T1] Core Prisma models and migrations: organiser, provider and consumer profiles linked to users, districts and categories (the users table comes from the auth set-up, EN-04)

[EN-03-T2] Data design document in the code repo: every table with its owner module, its database (PostgreSQL or DynamoDB) and its PRD IDs; DynamoDB keys designed from their reads before the tables are built (table creation plan)
[EN-03-T3] Prisma seed script for local and dev databases: fake demo accounts and events in Colombo, Kandy and Galle

[EN-03-T4] Schema rules written down: PostgreSQL tables change only through Prisma migrations and DynamoDB tables only through the CDK code, never by hand in DBeaver or the AWS console; hosted databases get prisma migrate deploy only (PRD section 8)

[EN-03-T6] Shared PostgreSQL 16 for the dev stage: choose the host (hosted PostgreSQL with a connection pooler such as Supabase or Neon, proposed), make the migrate and app database users, pooled and direct connection strings, run prisma migrate deploy
[EN-03-T7] DynamoDB tables in the CDK code: chat messages, feed items and WebSocket connections, on-demand capacity, time to live where data expires; keys from the table creation plan (proposed)

[EN-04-T1] Cognito as Amplify Gen 2 code in amplify/auth (already in the repo): email or phone sign-in; groups attendee, organiser, vendor, freelancer and admin; pre-sign-up and post-confirmation functions; review and test it
[EN-04-T2] NestJS AuthGuard (aws-jwt-verify checks the Cognito access token) and RolesGuard (role from the Cognito group, never from the request body) on every route; owner checks in each service
[EN-04-T3] Amplify Flutter auth library in the app against the same Cognito pool: sign-in, session storage, auth state, and the access token sent on every API call (proposed)
[EN-04-T4] Amplify Auth in Next.js (ConfigureAmplify with amplify_outputs.json for each stage); protected and admin-only routes; the access token sent to the API
[EN-04-T5] Limits on sign-in attempts and code requests: Cognito's built-in limits plus a per-number cap on SMS codes (proposed)

[EN-04-T6] users table (Prisma): Cognito sub, email, phone, role copied from the group, status; contact CHECK rules; row made on the first request; GET /me (built in the auth set-up run, 19 Nov 2026; review and merge)
